ai.description: The Eastern Trinket Snake reaches 1.5 meters. It is olive-brown with dark, black-edged crossbars and a distinct black stripe extending behind each eye. The body is slender with a keeled, triangular head.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Eastern Trinket Snake is best identified by the distinct, narrow black "teardrop" mark extending vertically downward from the bottom of each eye.
ai.habitat: The Eastern Trinket Snake inhabits dense subtropical forests and hilly terrain in the Himalayas and Northeast India, typically ranging from 500 to 2,500 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The Eastern Trinket Snake is primarily diurnal and exhibits a distinct defensive display by flattening its neck and vibrating its tail when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Elaphe cantoris* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the spring and summer months in its native Indian range.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Elaphe cantoris* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, ranging from Sikkim and West Bengal to Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
